header: IN THE PESHAWAR HIGH COURT, ABBOTTABAD
body: Date of hearing……………….24.09.2026…………………………... Petitioner (Saeed Ahmad Awan) By Mr. Sajjad Ahmad Abbasi, Advocate.

Respondents (Shah Abdul Raheem & others) Respondents No.1 & 2 By Sardar Aamir Qadir, Advocate. ******************* MUHAMMAD TARIQ AFRIDI, J.- Through this common judgment, I intend to dispose of the instant writ petition as well as the connected writ petition bearing No.479-A/2025, as both arise from separate judgments dated 04.03.2025 passed by the learned Additional District Judge-VII, Abbottabad, whereby the revision petitions preferred by the respondents against the order dated 25.11.2024 passed by the learned Civil Judge-II, Abbottabad, were allowed, and consequently the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 11.05.2017 was set aside and the suit was restored with directions to the learned trial court to proceed in accordance with law.

2. Brief facts are that the petitioner/plaintiff instituted a civil suit for recovery of Rs.30,00,000/- (rupees thirty lac) along with profit in terms of deeds dated 30.09.2012 and 01.02.2013, besides damages of Rs.5,00,00,000/- (rupees five crore). The respondents/defendants were proceeded against ex-parte, and the suit was decreed vide judgment and decree dated 11.05.2017 to the extent of Rs.30,00,000/- (rupees thirty lac) along with 15% profit, whereas the claim for damages was dismissed. Subsequently, the respondents/ defendants filed separate applications dated 06.06.2024 seeking setting aside of the said exparte decree, which were duly contested by the petitioner/plaintiff through filing of written replies. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties, the learned trial Court, vide order dated 25.11.2024, dismissed the said applications. Feeling aggrieved, the respondents preferred separate revision petitions before the learned Revisional Court, which were allowed through separate judgments dated 04.03.2025, hence, these constitutional petitions.

4. The controversy requiring determination is whether, in the circumstances of the case, the respondents’ applications for setting aside the exparte decree could properly be decided without framing material issues, including those relating to limitation and non-affixation of the requisite fee, and without affording the parties an opportunity to lead evidence. A perusal of the applications, the replies thereto and the decisions of the courts below reveals that the controversy involved various disputed questions of fact and was not confined to a pure question of law. The reasons for the respondents’ non-appearance, the circumstances which prevented them from contesting the suit, the date and manner of their acquiring knowledge of the ex-parte decree, and their explanation for approaching the Court approximately seven years after its passing required proper examination. Likewise, the petitioner/plaintiff had a vested right arising out of the decree passed in his favour and was entitled to controvert those assertions and produce evidence in support of their objections.

5. It is an admitted position that the learned trial Court, while deciding the applications for setting aside the ex-parte decree, neither framed issues arising out of the pleadings of the parties, nor afforded them an opportunity to lead evidence in support of their respective stands. Instead, it decided the applications on the basis of pleadings and oral submissions of the learned counsel, who referred to the documents that had neither been brought on record nor exhibited through the examination of the official concerned. In view of the disputed factual foundation of the applications, such procedure was not sufficient for effective adjudication of the controversy, particularly when the applications were filed approximately seven (07) years after the decree affecting the valuable rights accruing the petitioners thereunder.

6. The provisions relating to setting aside of an ex-parte decree are founded upon the principle of balancing the right of a litigant to contest the proceedings with the decree-holder’s interest in the finality of litigation. The grounds invoked for reopening the proceedings must, therefore, be examined on a proper factual foundation.

7. In the present case, the delay of about seven years in filing the applications for setting aside the ex-parte decree warranted closer scrutiny by the learned trial Court. The respondents were required to explain their absence throughout the proceedings and their prolonged inaction following the decree. The petitioner, on the other hand, was entitled to contest that explanation furnished by the respondents and demonstrate the effect of such delay upon his accrued rights. These questions could only be resolved after framing of appropriate issues and recording evidence from both sides. Appropriate issues were, therefore, necessary to enable both sides to substantiate their respective pleas.

8. The learned Revisional Court, while exercising revisional jurisdiction failed to address this procedural deficiency and proceeded to decide the controversy on merits without the requisite factual inquiry. In these circumstances, the appropriate course was to remit the applications to the learned trial court for adjudication after framing the necessary issues and recording evidence.

9. This Court is, therefore, of the considered view that the decisions of the courts below, cannot be sustained as dispute questions of fact were determined without a proper inquiry. The ends of justice demand that the parties should be afforded a fair opportunity to establish their respective pleas before the learned trial Court.

10. Consequently, the instant and connected constitutional petition bearing No. 479-A/2025 are allowed. The impugned judgments dated 04.03.2025 passed by the learned Additional District Judge-VII, Abbottabad, as well as the order dated 25.11.2024 passed by the learned Civil Judge-II Abbottabad are set aside. The respondents’ applications for setting aside the exparte Judgment and decree dated 11.05.2017 are remanded to the learned Civil Judge-II, Abbottabad, for a fresh decision strictly in accordance with law, after framing the necessary issues arising from the pleadings of the parties including the question of limitation and after providing adequate opportunity to both sides to produce their respective pro and contra evidence.

11. The learned trial Court shall decide the matter independently, on the basis of evidence brought on record and the applicable law. All questions concerning limitation and the grounds for setting aside the ex-parte decree shall remain open for determination. The observations made herein are confined to the procedural deficiency necessitating remand and shall not be construed as an expression of opinion on the merits of either party’s case.

12. The learned trial Court is directed to make all possible efforts to conclude the proceedings expeditiously, preferably within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment. The parties are directed to appear before the learned trial court on 08.10.2026. Announced:
